page: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz, accompanied by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 4.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of general-purpose profiles. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage solutions, and features a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the dedicated Zen 4 core demonstrates upper-quartile single-threaded performance, recording a stress-ng single-core score of 3031.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1955.0. Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics sit in the lower percentiles due to the single-vCPU limitation, as reflected by a multi-core Geekbench score of 1956.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 2667.55.

The hardware configuration provides an economical entry point to AMD EPYC Gen7 performance without the resource overhead of multi-core allocations. Its strong single-thread throughput and modern DDR5 memory make it appropriate for lightweight background jobs, microservices, small web applications, and low-scale developmental databases, whereas parallelized computing and throughput-heavy I/O workloads will be constrained by the single-thread ceiling and lack of local storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is a general-purpose instance featuring a single dedicated core from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 4.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, the instance delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. It includes no integrated local storage and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, ranking in the top quartile for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, total compute throughput remains constrained by the single-vCPU ceiling, placing multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics in lower tiers. The instance provides an efficient hardware baseline for small microservices, development environments, and lightweight web serving.
